subject: Agriculture
title: Breeds and Selective Breeding
description: A fast breakdown of Breeds and Selective Breeding for builders.

hook.text: A Holstein cow produces 10,000 liters of milk per year. A wild aurochs produced enough for one calf.

buildup.text: Centuries of selective breeding transformed cattle into specialized machines—some for milk, some for meat.

discovery.text: Robert Bakewell pioneered systematic breeding in 18th-century England, selecting and isolating desired traits.

twist.text: Extreme specialization made breeds vulnerable. The average Holstein is inbred to a degree that concerns geneticists.

climax.text: Just six bull lines sired most of America's dairy cattle. Genetic diversity has collapsed.

punchline.text: We bred perfection into cattle—and diversity out.

quiz.question: Who pioneered systematic livestock selective breeding?
